script:
Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Friday, November 13. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 4 degrees Celsius, clear skies. The high will be 13 and the low 4 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 0 percent.

You have no appointments scheduled in the next 24 hours.

Now, the top 5 stories in AI today.

First, from The Verge: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen model across Search and Gemini app. Google has released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new AI model replacing 3.8 Flash, designed to better handle complicated questions including multi-part queries, typos, and highly specific requests. The model can break down questions and address each component in its responses. It is available starting immediately across Google Search, the Gemini app, and all tiers of Google's AI offerings. Why it matters: Major model release from Google that immediately affects search and AI applications used by consumers and enterprises.

Second, from TechCrunch: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal and congressional investigation. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned amid a scandal involving an alleged affair with a Chinese spy and a third reported affair with an Nvidia employee, according to Reuters. The resignation has triggered Democratic congressional investigations into Nvidia's China sales and dealings with Trump, with national security implications for the U.S.-China AI infrastructure race. Why it matters: Leadership upheaval at Nvidia, the central supplier of AI infrastructure, has broad industry and geopolitical consequences.

Third, from TechCrunch: Nebius plans $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion. Nebius is pursuing a $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion funded through customer prepayments and loans, following the 'neocloud' playbook. The plan comes amid questions about its financing model, including delays at a Microsoft data center. The scale of proposed spending signals continued massive investment in AI compute infrastructure outside the traditional hyperscalers. Why it matters: Major AI infrastructure buildout indicating sustained capital investment in AI compute capacity beyond the largest cloud providers.

Fourth, from OpenAI: Amplitude deploys OpenAI-powered product agent Wave. Amplitude has deployed a proactive product agent called Wave, built primarily on OpenAI models, that identifies what to build, helps engineering teams ship changes using coding agents, and measures business impact. The company says it now ships product improvements in one to two days. The agent represents an end-to-end AI application for product development workflows. Why it matters: Practical enterprise AI agent automating product management and software delivery cycles.

Fifth, from Ars Technica: FAA expands AI advice for U.S. air traffic congestion. The FAA has expanded AI-generated advice to manage air traffic congestion across the entire U.S. airspace, extending the tool beyond previous limited deployments. Airlines have praised the tool, though the air traffic controllers' union was not involved in the rollout. The expansion marks a significant widening of AI deployment in critical national aviation infrastructure and air traffic management. Why it matters: Practical AI deployment in safety-critical national infrastructure affecting commercial aviation.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
